observations: The retained historical evidence records twenty successful initial predictions and twenty-five successful top-five ensemble predictions.
NB13_E104Q ranked first and had no severe-clash ensemble model.
interpretation: NB13_E104Q is the leading computational candidate under the retained scoring method.
limitations: No wet-lab affinity, specificity, expression, stability, or functional validation was performed.
Model confidence and ranking scores are not experimental binding measurements.
The exact Boltz package version used for the historical result snapshot was not retained; fresh predictions may differ after software, model, MSA, hardware, or stochastic changes.

actual_tools: Boltz-2 in a completed local GPU run
Python and Gemmi scoring scripts retained with the public case
execution.device: local GPU compute for the retained scientific results; local workstation for launcher observation and evidence inspection
execution.implementation: retained public-target KN035 design and Boltz-2 ensemble results plus a separately recorded Rosalind launcher observation; no Rosalind scientific job executed

provenance.note: The scientific outputs come from a separately completed Boltz-2 GPU run. Public sequences and portable preparation, execution, and scoring scripts support a fresh rerun. outputs/rosalind-open-observation.json records only the genuine mcp__rosalind__rosalind_open launcher call and explicitly states that it executed no scientific job.

reproduction: Verify the retained PD-L1 sequence against UniProt Q9NZQ7 residues 18-239 and the KN035 parent against PDB 5JDS.
Generate all 20 YAML inputs, run the fixed-seed initial screen, rank it, resample the fresh top five, and score the ensemble using the commands in README.md.
Record current package versions and compare the fresh result with the retained snapshot while allowing for software, MSA, hardware, and stochastic drift.
Treat the Rosalind launcher observation separately from every Boltz computation.
